areas_of_law: Statutory interpretation (Crown Liability and Proceedings Act, s. 32)
issues: Whether s. 32 of the Crown Liability and Proceedings Act incorporates the limitation period of the province where the cause of action arose, rather than a separate federal six-year period, for Crown proceedings to recover a debt
Whether the provincial (e.g. two-year) limitation period applies to bar the employer's recovery of the salary overpayment where the relevant events occurred in that province

When the limitation period began to run — i.e., when the overpayment/debt was discoverable by the employer or employee, and whether discoverability principles under the applicable provincial limitations statute apply
Whether the employer's demand and payroll deductions three years after the overpayment, absent earlier acknowledgment or partial payment, restart or otherwise affect the limitation clock
Whether unilateral payroll deduction to recover an alleged overpayment is itself a legally authorized recovery mechanism for a federal separate employer, independent of the limitation period question

Whether the source of funds (Consolidated Revenue Fund) or the fact the debt is owed to a federal entity is legally relevant to which limitation period applies, given s. 32 CLPA's choice-of-law approach
key_facts: Client is an employee of a federal separate employer (federal public sector)
She went on sick leave after serious illness; paid sick leave credits were exhausted partway through the leave
She should have moved to leave without pay but pay system errors caused continued biweekly pay deposits for about two more months
Employer waited almost three years before notifying her it would recover the overpayment
Employer began deducting small amounts from each pay cheque to recover the debt
Employee lived and worked in the same province as the employer's headquarters and its compensation/pay administration function, and the author of the recovery demand was based there
Employer asserts it is a national organization, that funds came from the federal Consolidated Revenue Fund, and the debt is owed to a federal entity
Dispute centers on whether a federal six-year limitation period or a shorter provincial limitation period governs the recovery action
causes_of_action: Crown/employer claim for recovery of salary overpayment (debt owed to the Crown)
Employee defence based on expiry of limitation period
candidate_statutes: Crown Liability and Proceedings Act, s. 32
search_terms: Crown Liability and Proceedings Act section 32
provincial limitation period applies to Crown
recovery of pay overpayment federal public service
Crown proceedings limitation period choice of law
needs_clarification: Which province is the employee's workplace/employer headquarters located in, since the applicable provincial limitation period (and its discoverability rules) under s. 32 of the Crown Liability and Proceedings Act depends on that province's law?
